messages.subject: Distance training field exercises?
parts:
Folks, and specifically distance-sampling educators

I'm looking for a relatively easy and quick to set up field exercise for a
university-level distance sampling lab. In the past, we've used a uniform
distribution of flagging 'birds' that students could shoot with laser
range-finders (we're working in open shrubland vegetation cover), with
differing densities by using different colors of flagging to denote
'species'. This worked fairly well, but providing a sufficient number of
realistically difficult to detect 'birds' to then analyze back in the lab
is an exhausting exercise in even moderately deep snow cover (we're in
Utah, western NA, and it been a good year for snow). Add the inevitable
trails leading to each flagging 'bird', and we sometimes get
unrealistically high detectability, which defeated the purpose of the lab -
to demonstrate distance sampling's utility on scenarios with moderate to
low detectability.

This year we're looking at both a limited amount set-up time and knee-deep
breakable crust. So I'm looking for help. Suggestions? I know many of
you have played these games before...

-Russ
